classification.difficultyReason: Combine horizontal projections to obtain the requested span; for the hexagon, derive suitable right triangles and their angles from regularity before assembling the full width.

content.prompt: Find the length $AB$ in these diagrams. Answer to 2 d.p.

spec.description: Triangle AB with an unlabelled apex, both sloping lengths and base angles, and a red dashed altitude with a black right-angle marker. Decorative blue boundary replaced by black.
spec.mathematics: Left side 10.6 m, right side 20 m, angles at A and B 70 degrees and 30 degrees. Supplied measurements are retained despite slight inconsistency.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens visible; no calculated lengths shown.

answer.worked:
Let $F$ be the foot of the perpendicular from the apex to $AB$.
$$\begin{align*}AF&=10.6\cos70^{\circ}\\FB&=20\cos30^{\circ}\\AB&=10.6\cos70^{\circ}+20\cos30^{\circ}\\AB&\approx20.95\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Source-shaped hexagon with six matching equality ticks, one 120-degree angle, bottom side 5 cm and red dashed AB. Coordinates reproduce the drawing without asserting that regularity is a given.
spec.mathematics: All six sides equal 5 cm; only the upper-right interior angle is explicitly specified. These givens alone do not uniquely determine AB.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens visible; no answer shown.

answer.worked:
The hexagon is regular, so each sloping side makes $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal.
$$\begin{align*}AB&=5\cos60^{\circ}+5+5\cos60^{\circ}\\AB&=2.5+5+2.5\\AB&=10.00\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
